evidence: Horace, Ep. 2.2.72: festīnat calidus mūlīs gerulīsque redēmptor, the contractor in a hurry

terms.gloss: the contractor who takes on a job
evidence: Cicero, Q. fr. 3.1.5: ejus operis … conductōrem
terms.comment: Cato and Cicero use it of building works.

phrases.latin: Dominus sum. In animō habeō domum novam aedificāre. Tū conductor es. Quid faciēs? Quem architectum commendās?
phrases.english: I’m the owner. I mean to build a new house. You’re the contractor. What will you do? Which architect do you recommend? (After Traupman’s colloquium on p. 162.)
I’ve got a hammer! (Theo, playing the contractor)

sources: Lewis & Short: redemptor · Lewis & Short: conductor · Lewis & Short: conductor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 162.
